content_hash.description: The format-2 content-hash preimage: sha256('obsvr:content/2' || 0x00 || u64be(len(prompt)) || prompt || u64be(len(response)) || response), fields as UTF-8 bytes, lengths in bytes. Format 1 was sha256(prompt + response), and a bare concatenation does not remember where the boundary was: the digest pairs below marked equal_under_legacy demonstrate the defect - two different attributions of the same bytes, one digest. The length prefixes make the preimage unambiguous by construction; the leading tag domain-separates this digest from every other sha256 in the SDK. Producers: sdk/src/proxy/chain-format.ts, sdk-python/obsvr/chain_format.py. Consumers: sdk/tests/unit/signing-vectors.test.ts, sdk-python/tests/test_signing.py.

cases.note: lengths count UTF-8 BYTES (2 each here), not code units - the one place the two runtimes could disagree

legacy_v1_events.description: The same two events signed under format 1 (sha256(prompt + response), no chain_format field, no format element in the signature payload). FROZEN FOREVER: chains signed before format 2 existed are existing evidence, and both verifiers must keep verifying them - explicitly, reporting chain_format 1, never silently under the format-2 rule. These are the pre-change vectors verbatim.

chain_verification.description: Chain-verification verdicts over the events above. Both verifiers (sdk/src/governance/verify-chain.ts and sdk-python/obsvr/verify_chain.py) build the chain from `events` (or `legacy_v1_events.events` when a case says `events: legacy_v1`), apply each case's mutations in order, verify, and must produce THIS verdict - identical valid/broken_at/reason/chain_format in both languages. A divergence is a release blocker: it means a customer's evidence verifies in one language and not the other.

mutation_ops.api_key: verify with this key instead of the fixture's api_key

cases.desc: the unmodified vectors verify, and the result names the format they verified under
editing content after signing breaks that event's signature

moving text across the prompt/response boundary while keeping the concatenation intact ('hello'/'world' -> 'hellow'/'orld') breaks a format-2 signature. This is the attack format 2 exists to close: the length prefixes put the boundary itself under the HMAC.
a fabricated signature does not recompute
a genuine chain does not verify under the wrong key
a jumped sequence number is a gap

cases.desc: a chain is one session, one process, one SDK build - no legitimate producer changes format mid-chain, so a later event declaring a different format is a break, not a negotiation

cases.desc: a newer format is not guessed at by an older verifier - fail closed, and report no format because none was established

stripping chain_format from a format-2 chain reroutes verification to the legacy rule, where a format-2 signature can never recompute: the formats share no valid signature, so a downgrade is a break, not a bypass
a chain signed before format 2 existed still verifies, and the result says which rule it verified under - never silently as a current chain

DOCUMENTED LIMIT of format 1, identical in both languages: the legacy digest is sha256(prompt + response), so re-splitting 'hello'/'world' as 'hellow'/'orld' preserves the concatenation and the signature still verifies. This is the defect format 2 closes. A format-1 chain therefore proves content-in-order but NOT the prompt/response attribution boundary - which is exactly why the verifier reports chain_format, so a consumer weighing legacy evidence knows what it does and does not bind. Pinned so the limit is a stated decision, not an oversight.
claiming format 2 on an event signed under format 1 fails: the recomputed format-2 payload never matches a format-1 signature

DOCUMENTED LIMIT, identical in both languages: verification proves the events it is given are genuine, in order, and unmodified - not that they are all of them. A suffix starting at seq_no 2 is internally consistent, and nothing inside an export says the session began at 1. Detecting a dropped prefix needs the session's known start (the server-side sequence guard and the sealed ledger). Pinned so the silence is a decision, not an oversight.
